phenotype_specificity.statement: Elevated urinary GHB is stated for all patients (cohort-level). Exome sequencing was done, but the paper does not report results for other genes.

quotes.quote: As the gold-standard biomarker, elevated GHB was detected in all patients by urinary organic acids analysis.
Patients were diagnosed with SSADHD according to increased levels of GHB and the pathogenic variants in ALDH5A1, among whom patients 1 ~ 9 have been reported as clinical case series by us [13].
Whole exome sequencing was performed on DNA samples from the proband and/or parents.

de_novo.statement: No de novo finding is stated. Methods say both parents were Sanger sequenced, but per-parent results are not given.

quotes.quote: To determine the variants’ locations, Sanger sequencing was performed on DNA samples from the proband and both of their parents.

functional.statement: Construct expressed transiently in HeLa cells (WT and non-transfected controls): protein expression 27.9% and enzyme activity 8.7%, stated as significantly decreased.

quotes.quote: Protein expression level was significantly decreased (c.983 C > A, 27.9%; c.1105 C > G, 39.3%; c.1274T > C, 22.2%), and the enzyme activity level (c.983 C > A, 8.7%; c.1105 C > G, 13.9%; c.1274T > C, 2.8%) was also significantly decreased.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Missense substitution (predicted p.(Ala328Asp)) in exon 6, in the region the paper assigns to the catalysis domain. The paper states a biallelic loss-of-function mechanism for this autosomal-recessive disorder.

quotes.quote: Autosomal-recessive disease follows a single mechanism: biallelic loss-of-function that leaves residual activity below the threshold required for normal physiology [29].

SSADHD—also known as 4-hydroxybutyric aciduria or γ-hydroxybutyric aciduria—is a rare autosomal-recessive disorder marked by markedly elevated levels of γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) and its metabolites [8].

notably, c.800T > G (p.V267G), c.865G > A (p.G289R), c.983 C > A (p.A328D), c.1105 C > G (p.R369G), c.1274T > C (p.L425P) and c.1529 C > T (p.S510F) were reclassified from VUS to pathogenic (Table 4).

Following ACMG/AMP guidelines, we accordingly assigned PVS1 (null variants), PM2/BA1/BS1 (allele frequency), PM3 (detected in trans), PP3/BP4 (in silico predictions), PP4 (phenotype specificity), and BP6 (supporting evidence of benign impact) to the 14 variants as appropriate (Table 4).

concerns: Both variants in patient 7 are gap candidates in this batch (G-ssadh-007 and G-ssadh-009); evidence that rests on the other allele (trans, case count) is shared between the two.
Methods state that patients 1 to 9 were reported earlier by the same group (ref. 13, a 2019 Chinese-language case series not in this batch); the same person may appear there.

Methods say both parents were Sanger sequenced to determine the variants' locations, but no per-parent genotype is reported for any patient; the compound-heterozygous label is therefore stated, not shown, in the text.
Supplementary Table 3 has a "Frequency" column (e.g. 1/26) whose denominator is not defined; it looks like a within-study count, not a population frequency, and should not be read as population data.
Seizures are recorded as "No" for patient 7 while the follow-up column records "Unexplained death"; the paper gives no cause of death.
